title: Create a Java object without calling its ordinary constructor
answer: Yes, certain mechanisms can create an object without executing that class's ordinary constructor during the new object's creation. Java deserialization is a standard example for `Serializable` classes: the serializable class's constructors are not run when its state is restored, though the first non-serializable superclass constructor is invoked. Cloning can also create a new object without running the class constructor in the normal way. Reflection with `Constructor.newInstance()` does invoke a constructor, so it is not an example of constructor bypass.
